clue.text: Trainee reporter capturing that lady's heavenly figure

indicators.note: to capture something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a cub reporter is a junior journalist learning the trade
the possessive pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A junior journalist photographs a woman's angelic statue or portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: A cub reporter is a standard term for a newspaper trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a winged angelic being, often painted as a chubby child in religious art.

clue.text: Very fine hotel supported by EasyJet, say

indicators.note: in a down entry, something supported sits on top of what holds it up, fixing the order

parts.note: H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
easyJet is an example of a budget carrier

explanation.surface: A smart hotel sponsored by a budget carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supported by' puts H on top of AIRLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairline crack or margin is extremely thin, as narrow as a hair.

clue.text: Coniferous tree Edward planted in Yorkshire town

indicators.note: something planted in soil sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A man called Edward planted a conifer in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planted' suits the tree in the surface but is the insertion signal; Redcar is a seaside town on the North Yorkshire coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The red cedar is a large North American conifer prized for its aromatic timber.

clue.text: Bird wailed periodically, circled by hunting dog

indicators.note: circled by means surrounded, so the kept letters go inside

parts.note: a beagle is a hound bred for hunting hares

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A bird kept screeching now and then as a hound circled it.
explanation.walkthrough: The kept letters go inside the dog's name straight after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The bald eagle is a large bird of prey, the national bird of the United States.

clue.text: Contemptuously dismiss pair of spinning rings

indicators.note: something spinning turns round, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: the pair means the same ring word is used twice

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at two hula hoops twirling round.
explanation.walkthrough: One ring word is turned round and then written twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To pooh-pooh an idea is to wave it away with scorn as unworthy of consideration.

clue.text: Inflammatory quality of Conservative, so badly under pressure

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters come out in a different order
in a down entry, being under something means coming below it, fixing the order

parts.note: the letters of these two words jumbled

explanation.surface: A Tory politician performing poorly under strain is being inflammatory.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'under pressure' means the jumbled letters sit beneath P.
explanation.definitionFit: Provocativeness is the trait of deliberately stirring up anger or strong reaction.

clue.text: Possibly steamed fruit for thrilling occasion

parts.note: something steamed is hot, 'possibly' because not everything hot is steamed
a date is a fruit of the palm

explanation.surface: A warmed fruit seems a dull treat, posing as a cookery note.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words switch sense: steamy fruit becomes an exciting romantic evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot date is an exciting romantic outing with someone attractive.

clue.text: Exaggerate the merits of lines at the end of old poetry

indicators.note: placed at the end means coming last, fixing where that piece goes

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
L is short for line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Overpraising a poem whose last lines are old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: L for line is a standard abbreviation, and doubling it makes the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversell something is to make exaggerated claims for its value or quality.

clue.text: Leader and Liberal politician welcoming a source of illumination

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A party leader and a Liberal MP greet someone bright with ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the politician does the welcoming, so the lone letter sits inside the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlamp is the lamp on a vehicle's front or worn on the head, giving light.

clue.text: Spicy food and French alcohol boy rejected, along with two doughnuts?

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: a ring doughnut looks like the letter O, so two give a pair of Os

explanation.surface: A lad turns down French wine but helps himself to doughnuts.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'doughnuts' are being used for their ring shape, the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindaloo is a fiercely hot curry from Goan cuisine, a staple of British Indian restaurants.

clue.text: Wise and divine female thus entertained by non-drinkers

indicators.note: a guest entertained by hosts is held within their home, so one piece goes inside another

explanation.surface: A clever, saintly woman is hosted by a group of teetotallers.
explanation.walkthrough: AA (Alcoholics Anonymous) is a standard crossword way to clue people who do not drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena is the Greek goddess of wisdom, so she is both wise and divine.

clue.text: Singer covering Queen, say — or Ziggy Stardust?

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so the other pieces sit inside

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice

explanation.surface: A vocalist does a cover of a Queen song, or perhaps a Bowie one.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests rock covers; Queen is ER, and the question mark marks Ziggy Stardust as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ziggy Stardust was the stage persona David Bowie adopted, a second self, which is what an alter ego is.

clue.text: Mother's energy low, initially — might she be in distress?

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother, with the possessive S

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: Mum feels drained and down, so is she in trouble?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the stock phrase for the maiden rescued in old romances.
explanation.definitionFit: A damsel in distress is the stock helpless young woman of fairy tales awaiting rescue.

clue.text: Beg Laura to get stirred up for debate

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone pleads with Laura to get angry and join the argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirred up' reads as one phrase, but 'up' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arguable is open to dispute, so still a matter that can be contested.

clue.text: Most of crude oil wasted by American — absurd!

indicators.note: most of means not all, so the final letter is dropped
wasted means ruined, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation at Americans squandering petroleum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude oil' reads as one phrase, but the first word is trimmed before both are jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludicrous means so foolish as to be laughable, the same as ridiculous.

clue.text: Endlessly study writer of a lot of nonsense

definitions.text: writer of a lot of nonsense

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A complaint about someone who studies forever while producing rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: LEARN loses its last letter, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear was the Victorian poet famed for nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat.

clue.text: Abandoned unfinished wine — good red, perhaps

indicators.note: unfinished means lacking its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A half-drunk bottle left behind, a good red wine at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like wine, but it means a socialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A red, meaning a communist or socialist, is an example of someone left-wing politically.

clue.text: A reason to go to the bookies, trembling

parts.words: reason to go to the bookies
parts.note: a flutter is a small bet, placed at a bookmaker's shop

explanation.surface: Someone nervously heads to the betting shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is British slang for a modest wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Aflutter means in a state of nervous excitement, quivering with agitation.

clue.text: 151 pence for something you could see on YouTube

definitions.text: something you could see on YouTube

parts.note: 151 in Roman numerals: C=100, L=50, I=1
p is the abbreviation for pence

explanation.surface: Paying a pound and a half for an online video.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman numerals turn 151 into CLI; P is the usual British shorthand for pence.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip is a short excerpt of video, the kind of thing posted on online video sites.

clue.text: Important person who reviews case of appeal

indicators.note: the case of something is its outside, so only the outer letters are kept

explanation.surface: A key reviewer looks at a legal appeal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of appeal' sounds legal but means the outside letters of appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Critical can mean crucial or decisive, as in a critical moment.

clue.text: Popular educational institutions working together

explanation.surface: Well-liked universities collaborating with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working together' reads as one phrase, but 'working' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things in unison means doing them simultaneously, all at once in agreement.

clue.text: Possibly bitter about untamed fox

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: bitter is a type of beer, so 'possibly' signals an example

explanation.surface: Perhaps a resentful feeling towards a wild fox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fox' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning to puzzle; bitter is an English style of ale.
explanation.definitionFit: To fox someone is to baffle them, the same as to confuse or perplex.

clue.text: Lions test match?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: large wild animals hunted for sport
second meaning: an important sporting fixture

explanation.surface: A rugby touring side playing an international fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The British and Irish Lions are a rugby team playing Test matches, but here lions are animals on safari.
explanation.definitionFit: Big game means large animals hunted for sport, and also an important, high-stakes match.

clue.text: Tread heavily in tango with Barnaby in a novel

parts.note: T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: Dancing a heavy-footed tango with a fictional character.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnaby needs the novel to fix his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge is to walk slowly and heavily, as if wearily plodding.

clue.text: Going out touring clubs is intoxicating

indicators.note: to tour is to go around, so one piece encircles the other

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for the card suit

explanation.surface: A night spent going round nightclubs is heady stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' are the card suit, not nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Intoxicating is used figuratively for something thrilling and exhilarating.

clue.text: Artist breaking strangely tiny item on a desktop

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of order, so these letters are rearranged
breaking into something means going inside it

explanation.surface: A painter oddly smashes a small object on the computer screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desktop' suggests a computer, but it is a real desk where paperwork waits.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-tray is a tray on an office desk holding incoming papers awaiting attention.

clue.text: One who performs a ritual live, caging mythical monster

indicators.note: to cage something is to enclose it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: an orc is a fantasy monster

explanation.surface: A priest performing a rite on stage while trapping a fabled beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' looks like the adjective (as in a live show) but is the verb, to be alive.
explanation.definitionFit: An exorcist performs a rite intended to drive out evil spirits.

clue.text: Beautiful stuff Vogue's oddly ignored

parts.note: to gorge is to stuff oneself

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters keeps only the even ones

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Lovely items in the fashion magazine are somehow overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S of Vogue's counts as a letter for the selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgeous means strikingly attractive, a strong synonym for lovely.

clue.text: Musical work about love and girl's final farewell

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around the others

parts.note: a song is a piece of music
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: final points to the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A love song as a girl's last goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: O and L go inside SONG.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is an informal way of saying goodbye.
